abstract: Metastatic heart tumours are rare. Most arise from lung, breast and renal cancerous primaries, soft-tissue sarcoma and malignant melanoma. We report the case of a 32-year-old policeman who presented to the emergency department very short of breath with a five-week history of weight loss and malaise. He was noted to have a mass in his right testicle, numerous 2-3 cm round shadows on chest X-ray (CXR) and a large mass within the right ventricular cavity. After much informed debate, the patient was treated solely with chemotherapy with the expectation of cure. We set out this argument and recommendations for future patients with this unusual problem.
abstract_ja: 転移性心腫瘍はまれである。大半は肺、乳房、腎臓の原発巣、軟部肉腫、悪性黒色腫に由来する。本稿では、5週間の体重減少と倦怠感を訴えて救急外来を受診した32歳男性警察官の症例を報告する。右精巣の腫瘤、胸部X線で多数の2-3cm大の円形陰影、右心室腔内の大きな腫瘤が認められた。慎重な議論の末、患者は治癒を期待して化学療法単独で治療された。本稿では、この稀な問題に関する議論と今後の患者に対する推奨事項を提示する。
